The 30-character gap between `zh-06` pptx and pdf is the table page: the pptx flattens cells with
`" | "`, the pdf joins them with spaces. Same content, different separator — not lost text.

Block types for the same two files:

```
en-01-sorting.pptx.json {'bullet': 27, 'table': 1, 'title': 10}
en-01-sorting.pdf.json  {'body': 5, 'bullet': 27, 'title': 10}
```

Five `body` blocks on the PDF table page are the five table rows read as text lines; the PDF path
keeps their geometry but not the cell grid (documented limitation, §5).

## 3. Gate results

```
> .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ruff check .
All checks passed!

> .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q
................                                                         [100%]
16 passed
```

`tests/test_ingest.py` (13 cases) asserts, per deck:

1. `test_manifest_covers_corpus` — manifest file set == files on disk.
2. `test_every_deck_has_ten_titled_pages` — 10 pages, page titles equal the corpus titles **exactly**, every page has text.
3. `test_document_title_comes_from_metadata` — deck title comes from PPTX core properties / PDF Info dict; `lang` is detected as `en`/`zh`.
4. `test_blocks_are_well_formed` — no empty block, bbox has positive width/height and stays inside the page.
5. `test_block_types_present` / `test_table_rows_are_structured` — bullets survive; the 5×5 table keeps its grid in PPTX.
6. `test_every_corpus_bullet_survives_ingest` — **every bullet of all 10 decks appears verbatim in its page text**, in both formats. This is the property B2 grounding depends on.
7. round-trip + CLI + error paths.

## 4. Three defects found and fixed while building this batch

These are the reason the batch is worth its time; each was a silent data-loss bug.

**(a) The PDF bullet glyph extracted as `\x00`.** `reportlab` rendered `•` with SimHei, which has no
U+2022; the missing glyph came back as NUL and the bullet was not recognised:

```
repr: '\x00 Split the array in half, sort each half recursively, then merge.'
```

Fix: draw the bullet with an Arial run (`bulletFontName`), and make `normalize()` strip control
characters defensively. Now: `'• Split the array ...'` → block type `bullet`.

**(b) SimHei silently dropped `−`, `∂`, `∇`, `ŷ`, `⌊`, `⌋`.** `2^h − 1` extracted as `2^h 1`:

```
assert '高度为 h 的二叉树最多有 2^h − 1 个结点。' in '... 最多有 2^h 1 个结点。 ...'
```

A lost minus sign would have produced a "verified quote" that says something different from the
slide. Fix: per-character font fallback (Cambria for the six codepoints) plus a hard glyph gate in
the generator — `_assert_glyph_coverage` aborts the build and names any character no font covers,
instead of emitting a lossy PDF.

**(c) `extract.json` files collided.** Naming output by `Path(source).stem` made `en-01-sorting.pdf`
overwrite `en-01-sorting.pptx`; the PDF JSON contained pptx data with `kind: "pptx"`. Fix: output is
named by the full file name (`en-01-sorting.pdf.json`).

## 5. Known limitations of this stage

- **PPTX bboxes are shape boxes, not per-line boxes.** python-pptx exposes shape geometry only, so
  four bullets in one text box share the same bbox. Page + quote is still exact; the box is coarse.
- **PDF tables are text, not grids.** `pdfplumber`'s line extractor yields rows as text; recovering
  cells needs `extract_table()` heuristics, which is out of scope for B1.
- **No OCR.** A scanned page yields an empty page with `flags.text_layer = false`; nothing in the
  corpus exercises that path yet.
- **Bullet detection in PDF is marker-based.** A PDF whose bullets are images or drawn shapes would
  yield `body` blocks; the pipeline only requires the text to be correct.

## 6. Reproduce

```powershell
.venv\Scripts\python.exe tools\gen_samples.py
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m lessonlens ingest eval/slides --out eval/extract --root .
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m ruff check .
.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_ingest.py -q
```
